title: Challenge Clichés
use_cases: Use when drafting narrative content to avoid overused tropes or predictable plot devices
Configure when establishing a unique authorial voice through original descriptions
Implement when revising dialogue to replace common idioms with descriptive language
Use when seeking to subvert genre expectations by turning standard reveals around
content: Two lovers literally bumping into each other. A single tear falling down someone’s cheek. Every chapter beginning with someone waking up. These examples are clichés that are easily avoidable by getting innovative and being conscious of what is and is not overdone. You can challenge clichés, like the “Scooby Doo reveal” where everyone is standing around in a circle as the villain is apprehended, by turning them around. Brainstorm original wording over idioms, such as “the rain hammered down to flood the streets” instead of “it was raining cats and dogs.” Or find other ways to surprise readers.
